text:
sophia: Heads up — onboarding ACME's LoRA merges. I tried merging acme/financial-lora:v3 onto redwood/longchat-7b-qlora-4bit and saw weird tokenization mismatches + hallucinations in the quick eval pack. Anyone run into this with 4-bit bases?
omar: hmm. did you run the model-compat check (scripts/compatibility/check_merge.py)?
sophia: ran it, output said 'param_shape_mismatch' on layer 10 and some tokenizer id mismatch. The LoRA was trained on a modified tokenizer (added <txn> token).
liam: Tokenizer differences will definitely break generation. Options: 1) remap new tokens to existing vocab, 2) patch tokenizer at serving time, 3) retrain LoRA with base tokenizer. Which is feasible for ACME?
maya: ACME prefers minimal retraining. They can accept a tokenizer patch if it's safe for downstream NER.
sophia: ok tried remapping by inserting the <txn> token id to the base vocab (quick hack) and re-merged. Behavior improved but eval metrics still off. Quick eval pack used: acme-qc-pack-v2 (50 examples).
bench-bot: quick-eval acme-qc-pack-v2 merged-on-4bit: exact_match 0.71 -> 0.64 (base 0.73), f1 0.82 -> 0.77, rouge-L 0.66 -> 0.61. Perplexity increased from 12.4 -> 18.7.
omar: those are meaningful regressions. Are you merging LoRA weights using the recommended merge script that supports 4-bit quant bases? e.g.:
```bash
python tools/merge_lora.py \
  --base-model redwood/longchat-7b-qlora-4bit \
  --lora acme/financial-lora:v3 \
  --out acme-merged-4bit-v1 \
  --mode=q4_0_compat
```
liam: also check that the LoRA was trained with respect to the same normalization (RMSNorm vs LayerNorm). That can cause distribution shifts after merge.
sophia: LoRA training logs: used layernorm_orig=true, rmsnorm=false. Base model uses rmsnorm. That mismatch could explain some of it.
rachel: Actionable plan: 1) run a compatibility diff to list norm & vocab mismatches, 2) produce a 100-example subset eval (more variety) and run merges with two strategies: a) tokenizer remap + normalization adapter b) convert LoRA to rmsnorm-compatible by reparameterizing small adapter.
maya: ACME ok with us trying adapter conversion — they want ETA before next week.
liam: infra-bot: spawned sandbox instance redwood-sbox-ml-42 (g4dnx2) for testing, /logs at s3://redwood-acme/merges/1763501234/
infra-bot: NOTE: GPU has 40GB free. Use the dedicated slot for heavier merges.
sophia: I'll run the reparameterize script tonight. If that fails, we can propose a small LoRA retrain. Sharing the quick diff I ran:
```diff
- tokenizer.add('<txn>')
+ tokenizer.map('<txn>') -> id 50250
```
omar: please also compute a cosine-sim of key activations before/after merge on a sample batch. If similarity < 0.85 that's a red flag.
sophia: preliminary cos-sim on last kv layer: 0.72 after naive merge. I'll post detailed logs after runs.
bench-bot: scheduled job 1763502000: acme-merge-reparam-1 queued (ETA ~45m).
rachel: Thanks — keep ACME & CS updated (maya). If reparam gets us within 95% of baseline metrics on the 100-ex eval, we can ship a patched merge + rollout to Dedicated for validation. If not, propose retrain + quick fine-tune plan and cost estimate.
maya: noted, I'll prepare ACME comms draft. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks all — I'll post results here when bench finishes.
